item.description: Tuesday 24 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS: não informado | An information disclosure vulnerability in Zstandard versions 1.5.1 through 1.5.7 allows specially crafted compressed data to expose the contents of an internal buffer through decompressed output. item.title: CVE-2026-130166 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.7
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.7 | n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Prior to 1.123.90 and 2.14.0, the invitation acceptance endpoint accepts inviter and invitee user IDs without a signed invitation token, allowing any preexisting member to take over a pending new user account. A member with permission to list users can read the ID of a pending account and set its password without authentication, then log in as that user, including as an admin when the invitation has the admin role. Exploitation requires an invitation that has not been accepted yet. This issue is fixed in versions 1.123.90 and 2.14.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-130167 - NVD - CVSS Score v4.0: 7.5
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v4.0: 7.5 | n8n is an open source workflow automation platform. Prior to 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2, the password reset link and role change operations do not protect the instance owner account from users with a custom instance role. A user whose custom instance role includes user management permissions can obtain a password reset link for the owner and take over the owner account, or change the owner's role, gaining full control of the instance. Exploitation requires the custom roles feature and a custom instance role with user management permissions. This issue is fixed in versions 2.47.6, 2.48.3, and 3.2.2.

item.title: CVE-2026-130169 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 10.0
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 10.0 | AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. In versions 0.6.26 through 0.7.4, AutoGPT Platform ships a publicly known, hardcoded default JWT verification key in backend/.env.default and autogpt_platform/.env.default. Because HS256 is symmetric, anyone who knows the secret can forge valid JWTs for any user or for the admin role, bypassing authentication and authorization without user interaction. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-132257 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 8.2
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 8.2 | AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. From versions 0.6.23 and above, before 0.8.0, AutoGPT Platform ships a hardcoded default Fernet encryption key in backend/.env.default, which encrypts every user's OAuth tokens, API keys, and integration credentials in the User.integrations column. Anyone with read access to the database of a deployment using the default key can decrypt the stored credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.8.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133455 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | AutoGPT is a workflow automation platform for creating, deploying, and managing continuous artificial intelligence agents. Prior to 0.9.0, nested tools invoked by OrchestratorBlock bypass the main execution queue and are charged only after succeeding, but post-run billing still refunds a failed tool's catalogue price as a presumed pre-flight charge. Any authenticated customer can trigger failed nested calls to add uncharged credits to their balance and fund later executions using the operator's credentials. This issue is fixed in version 0.9.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-133930 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 5.3 | A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests. An authenticated user with read access to an index who requests Arrow output containing an affected column type can receive data from indices they are not authorized to access. A temporary block can be released to a shared memory pool before deferred response writers finish using it, allowing concurrent requests to reuse the same memory. The attacker cannot select which concurrent data is disclosed.

item.title: CVE-2026-134020 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.5 | OpenEMR is a free and open source electronic health records and medical practice management application. Prior to 8.5.0, the staff-facing portal endpoints GET api/onsiteactivityviews and GET api/onsiteactivityview/{id}, mapped to OnsiteActivityView.Query and OnsiteActivityView.Read with p_acl = p_none in portal/patient/_app_config.php, are handled without an authorization check for an authenticated staff session whose bootstrap_pid is empty. portal/patient/_machine_config.php admits that authenticated staff session, and portal/patient/fwk/libs/verysimple/Phreeze/GenericRouter.php applies the route ACL only when bootstrap_pid is nonempty, so the staff request bypasses the p_none check. OnsiteActivityViewController::Query() returns records without patient scoping, and OnsiteActivityViewController::Read() loads a record by identifier without checking ACL or ownership; OnsiteActivityViewReporter::GetCustomQuery() joins portal activity to patient demographics and includes names, dates of birth, addresses, and Social Security numbers. Any authenticated staff account, including one without the patients/demo permission, can therefore read sensitive demographics for patients represented by an existing onsite_portal_activity row; at least one such row must exist for the endpoint to return patient data. This issue is fixed in version 8.5.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-134021 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.5 | TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.3.1, the Mollie payment notification handler in src/Payments/Mollie.php, processNotifyUrl(), uses a payment ID supplied with the notification to retrieve a paid transaction but does not verify that the transaction's order reference matches the order identified by the notification URL or that the transaction amount matches the order total. An ordinary customer can use a paid Mollie transaction from one order to cause a different, higher-value order to be marked paid without paying its full price. The endpoint is intentionally unauthenticated so Mollie's servers can reach it, and the request's order hash alone does not bind the fetched payment to that order. This issue is fixed in version 4.3.1.

item.title: CVE-2026-134022 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 3.7 | TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, the User extension’s onRequestResetPassword() handler in src/Http/Controllers/Login.php calls resetPassword() and mailSendResetPasswordRequest() only when an account matches. The resulting database write and reset-email send take longer than the nonexistent-account path despite the endpoint returning the same response, allowing timing measurements against a production deployment using a synchronous queue and real SMTP transport to disclose valid staff or customer email addresses. The advisory’s local log-mailer test showed no measurable timing difference, so the signal depends on mail configuration and is useful for follow-on phishing or credential stuffing rather than direct account access. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-134023 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 7.4
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 7.4 | TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.2.0, checkResetPasswordCode() in src/Auth/Models/User.php compares a submitted reset code with the stored 42-character token using a normal string comparison, which can return after the first differing byte instead of taking constant time. The password-reset flow exposes this comparison to remote requests, but the endpoint is rate-limited to six requests per minute per IP, and the advisory reports no live exploit or practical token-recovery demonstration. Recovering a high-entropy reset code through the constrained timing signal could permit an unauthorized password reset. This issue is fixed in version 4.2.0.

item.title: CVE-2026-134024 - NVD - CVSS Score v3.1: 6.8
item.description: Monday 23 November 2026 | NVD | CVSS Score v3.1: 6.8 | TastyIgniter is an open-source online ordering, table reservation, and restaurant management system. Prior to 4.4.4, addFromUrl() in src/Flame/Database/Attach/Media.php performs an outbound HTTP request to a caller-supplied URL and stores the response without validating the URL scheme or destination, which could enable server-side request forgery if a reachable feature passes attacker-controlled URLs to the method. The maintainer reports that no shipped first-party feature calls this method and that it is currently unreachable through product functionality, so no current attack path or impact was identified. This issue is fixed in version 4.4.4.
